it-2004-it-70.approach: The lines of code $L$ are fixed, so $E^{1/3}t^{4/3}$ must stay constant. Cubing gives $E\,t^4=$ constant, so halving the duration multiplies effort by $2^4=16$.

steps.title: What stays constant
steps.body:
$L=P\,(E/B)^{1/3}\,t^{4/3}$ with $L,P,B$ fixed $\Rightarrow E^{1/3}t^{4/3}=\text{const}$.

Cube both sides: $E\,t^{4}=\text{const}$.

steps.title: Scale the effort
steps.body: $E_2=E_1\left(\dfrac{t_1}{t_2}\right)^4=20\times\left(\dfrac{8}{4}\right)^4=20\times16=320$ person-months.

optionAnalysis.reason: 10 assumes effort scales with duration ($E\propto t$); compressing the schedule increases effort.
40 treats $E\propto 1/t$ (only a factor 2).
160 uses $(8/4)^3=8$; after cubing, the exponent of $t$ is 4.

pitfalls: Cubing $t^{4/3}$ gives $t^4$, not $t^3$.
it-2004-it-70.verification: Check: $320\cdot4^4=320\cdot256=81920$ and $20\cdot8^4=20\cdot4096=81920$ — equal, so $L$ is unchanged.

steps.body: A23 cannot stay in E2 (it would break 1NF), so it gets $E2\_A23(\underline{A21, A23})$.

steps.title: Count
steps.body: $E1,\ E2,\ E2\_A23\Rightarrow 3$ tables, each in 3NF.

it-2004-it-77.approach: Build the precedence graph from conflicting pairs. A cycle rules out conflict serializability; a quick view check (who reads what, final writers) confirms that neither serial order is equivalent.

steps.body:

$W_2(A)$ before $W_1(A)$ ⇒ $T2\to T1$.

scene.caption: Two opposite edges from item A

steps.title: Cycle
steps.body: $T1\to T2\to T1$ is a cycle ⇒ S is not conflict serializable.

steps.title: View check
steps.body:
In S both transactions read the initial A; the final writer of A is T1 and of B is T2.

- Serial $T1,T2$: T2 would read the A written by T1 — differs.
- Serial $T2,T1$: T1 would read the A written by T2 — differs.

So S matches neither order (T2's update of A is lost).

optionAnalysis.reason: Edge $T2\to T1$ (and T2 reading the initial A) contradicts T1 running first.
Edge $T1\to T2$ (T1 reads the initial A) contradicts T2 running first.
A schedule whose precedence graph has a cycle cannot match both orders.
Cycle in the precedence graph, and the view test fails for both orders.

pitfalls: Only conflicting operations (same item, at least one write, different transactions) create edges.
it-2004-it-77.verification: Lost update: T1 overwrites A with a value computed from the old A, discarding T2's write — impossible in any serial run.

it-2004-it-81.approach: To keep old and new frames distinguishable, the sender's outstanding window and the receiver's acceptance window must never overlap in sequence space, so at least $N+M$ numbers are needed.

steps.title: Worst case
steps.body: The sender sends N frames, all received, but every ACK is lost. The receiver has advanced its window by N and now accepts M new numbers, while the sender retransmits the old N.

max(M,N) lets a retransmission fall inside the receiver's new window.

pitfalls: Special cases: Go-Back-N ($M=1$) needs $N+1$; Selective Repeat ($M=N$) needs $2N$ — both equal $M+N$.
it-2004-it-81.verification: Agrees with the known Go-Back-N and Selective Repeat bounds.

it-2004-it-82.approach: With a single sender, each frame cycle = transmit the frame, wait for its last bit to come back round the ring (removal), then release the token, which must travel round the ring once to come back.

Cycle $=1600\,\mu s$.

pitfalls: The token must return to the only active host before its next frame.
